glosses: to dare (be brave enough to do something)
To make (something) last for more time than is necessary; to prolong; to extend.

examples.text: It seems the boss tries to draw out these meetings for as long as possible just to punish us.

glosses: To physically extract, as blood from a vein.

examples.text: Orion hit a rabbit once; but though sore wounded it got to the bury, and, struggling in, the arrow caught the side of the hole and was drawn out. Indeed, a nail filed sharp is not of much avail as an arrowhead; you must have it barbed, and that was a little beyond our skill.

glosses: To extract, to bring out, as concealed information; to elicit; to educe.
To use means to entice or force (an animal) from its hole or similar hiding place.

examples.text: They used raw meat to draw the beast out of the cave.

glosses: To cause (a shy person) to be more open or talkative.

examples.text: She's really a neat person if you just take the time to draw her out.

glosses: To improve a losing hand to a winning hand by receiving additional cards.

examples.text: Jill had a flush on the turn, but Jimmy drew out by completing a full house on the river.

glosses: To leave the place (of an army), etc.
